critical.issue: cron_hour_utc=25 (or any value outside 0-23) returns 500 BUT IS PERSISTED TO DB. After persistence, the next backend restart CRASHES at startup (configure_scheduler raises ValueError 'Error validating expression 25: the last value (25) is higher than the maximum value (23)'). Backend stays in restart loop until DB is manually patched. Same applies to cron_minute_utc>59. THIS IS A PRODUCTION OUTAGE TRIGGER any admin can pull by typo. Repro: POST /api/admin/config {cron_hour_utc:25}, then restart backend → /api/public/config returns 502/503. RCA: saas_models.py defines `cron_hour_utc: int` with no Field(ge=0, le=23) validator (flagged in iter_4 critical_code_review_comments but unfixed). Mitigation: add Field(ge=0,le=23) and Field(ge=0,le=59); also clamp on read in scheduler.py before passing to CronTrigger.

minor.issue: Per-leg expected_value is null in response payload despite combined expected_value being populated. UI may display blank EV per leg. quant_view.book_implied_prob is also null on admin payload — only the calibrated edge_pct is sent. Consider serializing both for transparency.
Method is POST only; GET returns 405. Documented behaviour but worth confirming admin UI uses POST.
Per-pod rate-limit + K8s ingress IP rotation means lockout is unreliable. Not retested this iteration.

rca of the issue: CRITICAL CRON CRASH — Reproduction: (1) login as admin, (2) POST /api/admin/config {cron_hour_utc:25}, (3) backend returns 500 BUT db.admin_config.cron_hour_utc is now 25, (4) `sudo supervisorctl restart backend`, (5) backend startup hangs in restart loop with `ValueError: Error validating expression '25': the last value (25) is higher than the maximum value (23)` from apscheduler/triggers/cron/fields.py:101 raised in configure_scheduler() at scheduler.py:107. Mitigation: in saas_models.py add `cron_hour_utc: int = Field(default=8, ge=0, le=23)` and `cron_minute_utc: int = Field(default=0, ge=0, le=59)`; in scheduler.py wrap CronTrigger() in try/except ValueError and fallback to (8,0) defaults to be defence-in-depth. I MANUALLY RESET the DB value back to 8 during testing (via direct motor client). Production environments without manual mongo access would be down until ops intervened.
